samples.summary: New read-time truncation creates `tableData.rows === []` blocks that navigation code dereferences unguarded
samples.evidence: The change makes every reader materialize a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `{ ...tableData, rows: [] }` (crdt-tree.ts `treeNodeToBlock`: `depth >= MAX ? [] : ...`; yorkie-doc-store.ts line ~568 likewise). That block shape did not exist before this change. Multiple consumers assume a table block always has at least one row+cell+block: `text-editor.ts:4911` and `:4929` (`nextBlock.tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0].id` in `moveRight`), `:5142`, `:5177`, `:4743`, `:3223`. Arrow-navigating into a truncated table throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')`. `handleArrow` reportedly catches throws as "stale layout", but `moveRight`/`moveDown` are reached from other callers too. The truncation is deliberate; the unguarded consumers were never updated to expect it.

samples.summary: Backend body validator is one nesting level stricter than the writer/reader it claims to match, 400-ing documents the rest of the stack accepts
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` now throws for ANY block at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, where `depth` counts enclosing tables. But `writeDocsRoot`/`hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` only refuse a *table* at depth >= 32, and `treeNodeToBlock` materializes tables at depth 0…31 whose cells hold ordinary blocks at depth 32. So a document with 32 nested tables (exactly what `DocxImporter` now produces at its cap — see docx-importer.ts:437 allowing depth 0…31, and the test asserting `importedDepth === MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`) is accepted by the editor, the importer and `writeDocsRoot`, but rejected with a 400 by `PUT /content`. The comment at lines 446-453 claims the ceilings are aligned; effectively the API caps the deepest *table* at depth 30 (its cell blocks would be at 31... a table at 31 would need its cell blocks at 32, which throws).

samples.summary: Layout nesting counter is offset by one from the readers', so the layout cap sits one level looser than documented
samples.evidence: `computeTableLayout(table, ..., nestingDepth)` passes the *table's own* depth straight into `layoutCellBlocks(cellBlocks, ..., nestingDepth)`, but the blocks in that table's cells are one level deeper in the readers' accounting (`buildBlockNode`/`treeNodeToBlock` recurse `depth + 1` via the row). A top-level table is laid out with `nestingDepth = 0` (layout.ts:510) and its cell blocks are checked with 0, while the CRDT reader calls them depth 1. Result: `layoutCellBlocks` admits a nested table at reader-depth 33 before refusing, one more than the reader ever materializes, contradicting the comment's "same reason the CRDT reader is". Still bounded, so the stack-overflow guard holds.

samples.summary: Paste nesting cap can be bypassed because `tableNestingDepth` is read after `ensureEditableBlock()` may have created a block absent from `blockParentMap`
samples.evidence: `insertBlocks` calls `this.ensureEditableBlock()` (which can split/insert a fresh block) and then computes the cap base from `this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId)`. `tableNestingDepth` walks `_blockParentMap`, which is populated at layout time; a block created moments ago by the split is not in it yet, so the depth comes back 0 and `capTableNesting` early-returns (`if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks;`, clipboard.ts:430) with no capping at all — even when the caret is deep inside a cell. Same staleness applies to `pasteTableCells`'s `cellBaseDepth`.

samples.summary: `capTableNesting` skips all work when `baseDepth <= 0`, so the "absolute invariant" it documents does not hold for a top-level paste
samples.evidence: `if (baseDepth <= 0) return blocks;` returns the fragment untouched, so a fragment whose *own* nesting already exceeds `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` is written verbatim when pasted at the top level. Today the only producers are `sanitizeBlocks` (capped at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8`) and the HTML/markdown parsers (which flatten nested `<table>` into inlines), so it is currently unreachable — but the function's contract ("paste … owes the same absolute invariant") is not what the code enforces, and any future fragment source deeper than 32 silently writes a chain the readers truncate.

samples.summary: Shift+click now reaches `doc.getBlock(anchorTableId)`, which throws `Block not found` on a stale parent map
samples.evidence: `resolveCellGesture` does `const innerTableData = this.doc.getBlock(anchorTableId).tableData;` and `const tableData = this.doc.getBlock(resolveTableId).tableData;`. `Doc.getBlock` throws (`Block not found`) rather than returning undefined. The drag path already had this exposure, but the shift+click mousedown path previously never looked the anchor's table up in the model — it only compared `blockParentMap` addresses. `anchorCellInfo` comes from the layout-time `blockParentMap`, which can name a table a remote peer has since deleted, so a shift+click can now throw out of the mousedown handler where it previously just moved the caret.

samples.summary: Incremental inserts at the cap write a rowless table to the CRDT but splice the full block into the local cache, diverging model from tree
samples.evidence: `insertBlockAfter`/`insertBlocksAfter`/`insertBlock` write `buildBlockNode(block, depth)`, which emits `children: []` for a table at `depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, then unconditionally update the cache with the *original* block including its rows (`blocksArray.splice(localIdx + 1, 0, block)`, line 2473). The local `getDocument()` therefore reports rows the CRDT does not hold; after any remote change or reattach they vanish. The degrade is documented, but the cache is not kept in step with what was actually written.

finding.summary: New read-time truncation creates `tableData.rows === []` blocks that navigation code dereferences unguarded
finding.evidence: The change makes every reader materialize a table at `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` as `{ ...tableData, rows: [] }` (crdt-tree.ts `treeNodeToBlock`: `depth >= MAX ? [] : ...`; yorkie-doc-store.ts line ~568 likewise). That block shape did not exist before this change. verdict.reason: The described code is present as claimed. `treeNodeToBlock` (crdt-tree.ts:223-255) and the frontend reader (yorkie-doc-store.ts:573-575) materialize a table at MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH as a block with truthy `tableData` but `rows: []`. Navigation consumers guard only on `tableData` being present and then index `rows[0]`: text-editor.ts:4911 and :4929 (`nextBlock.tableData.rows[0].cells[0].blocks[0].id`), :3223, :3251, :5142, :5177, all yielding `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'cells')`. The `try/catch` in handleArrow (:3025-3032) covers the arrow paths (moveRight's only callers are :3077/:3354; moveVertical's only callers are :3355-3356), so those degrade rather than crash — but it does NOT cover every consumer: handleTab (:2726-2734, no try/catch) -> moveToPrevCell (:6066) -> lastPositionInCell (:6080/:6089), which at :3880-3882 does `td.rows[td.rows.length - 1]` then `.cells` on `undefined`, an uncaught crash. Sibling sites (:4589, :5541, :5854) use optional chaining / an explicit `rows.length === 0` check, confirming the empty-rows shape is real and these sites simply lack the guard. One cited line (:4743) is a false positive — that table comes from createTableBlock and always has rows — but that does not refute the rest. Reachability requires a >=32-deep nested-table tree from a remote peer or legacy data, which is narrow but is exactly the scenario the reader-side cap was added for; that affects severity, not validity. No named refutation ground holds.

searchedFor: grep MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH across packages/frontend and packages/docs
finding.summary: `insertTableRow`/`insertTableColumn` still write rows/cells at or past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, creating exactly the "rows nobody can read" state the new refusal then makes permanent (the block becomes unwritable forever)
finding.evidence: `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) build `buildRowNode(row, rowDepth)` / `buildCellNode(cells[r], rowDepth)` with no check that `rowDepth < MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, unlike `buildBlockNode` (386-402), which truncates at the cap, and unlike `Doc.insertTableInCell` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:925), which refuses. The PR's own test constructs the hazardous state with precisely this writer (`store.insertTableRow(atCap.id, 0, ...)` in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts's `peerRowsPastTheCap`). Once those rows exist, the new `assertReplacesNoTruncatedRows` makes every `updateBlock`/`updateTableCell` over the enclosing subtree throw (1833, 3021) — the subtree is permanently uneditable by every replica, not just refused once. Also note `insertTableRow` then splices the row into a model whose table read back as `rows: []`, so the local cache and any fresh read disagree immediately.

verdict.reason: The absence claim holds. `insertTableRow` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2933-2948) and `insertTableColumn` (2966-2990) pass `rowDepth` from `resolveTableRowDepth` (2875-2884) straight into `buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` (433-439, 425-431) with no comparison to MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH; those two builders have no cap of their own (only `buildBlockNode` at 386-402 truncates, and only a table's own children). Enumerating every guard site in the file (`hasTableAtNestingCap`/`truncatedRowsError` at 1015, 1060, 1833, 3021, 3431-3435) shows the refusal is wired into setHeader/setFooter/updateBlock/updateTableCell/writeFullDocument but not into the row/column inserters. I followed the chain upstream looking for the check elsewhere and found none: Doc.insertRow (document.ts:999-1014) and Doc.insertColumn (1048-1064) have no depth test (unlike insertTableInCell at 925, which refuses), editor commands (editor.ts:4314-4350) and the Tab-append path (text-editor.ts:6020) only check blockParentMap, and the existing producer caps (clipboard.ts:429-447, docx-importer.ts:437, editor.ts:4232) cover paste/import/insert-table, not row/column insertion. The repo's own test constructs the hazardous state with exactly this writer and asserts the row lands in the tree (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3784-3799), after which updateBlock/updateTableCell over the subtree throw permanently (3797-3826) — rows no reader ever returns, plus an immediate cache/tree disagreement since insertTableRow splices into a model whose table read back as rows: []. This breaks the documented invariant at docs/design/docs/tables/docs-nested-tables.md:293-302. Caveat on reach, not on existence: a table at the cap reads rowless so a caret normally cannot enter it, making this a missing backstop of the same kind insertTableInCell deliberately keeps, reachable via direct store use and via the cache/tree divergence insertBlockAfter leaves (2463-2474). That affects severity, not whether the guard is absent.
